title: Quiet, Lord, My Froward Heart
description: Quiet, Lord, My Froward Heart in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 234, “For a Childlike Spirit”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Qui-et, Lord, my fro-ward heart; Make me lov-ing, meek, and mild, Up-right, sim-ple, free from art; Make me as a lit-tle child; From dis-trust and en-vy free; Pleased with all that plea-seth Thee.

lines: Make me loving, meek, and mild,
Make me as a little child;
Pleased with all that pleaseth Thee.
Let me as a child receive;
Why should I the burden bear?
On a care beyond his own,
So would I with Thee abide,
Thou my Father, Guard, and Guide!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
